correctness.rationale: For any connected q-vertex marked subtree S and m=n-q outsiders, the Cayley forest-extension count gives exactly \(q n^{m-1}\) completions; imposing r distinct outsider-to-marked edges gives \((q+r)n^{m-r-1}\). The joint factorial moments are \((m)_{\underline r}(q+r)/(q n^r)\), valid even at r=m, and finite polynomial expansion gives ((m+sum_i z_i)/n)^(m-1)*(sum_i z_i/q). Factorization proves independent multinomial plus one-hot uniform category. Distinct-coordinate covariance equals \(-(m-1)/n^2-1/q^2\). The exact endpoint marginal agrees with the published one-endpoint law. An explicit projective coupling makes both endpoint degrees simultaneously nonincreasing as distance grows; each mean decreases strictly. The checker independently reconstructs every Prüfer tree through n=8 and verifies 648 exact rational coefficient, path-count and covariance statements. Finite enumeration is a check, not the all-n proof.

originality.rationale: The original item is the entire multivariate conditional distribution along a fixed subtree or path and associated pair dependence, not the classic forest-extension count or already published one-endpoint marginal. The closest full-text published source gives the marginal Bin+Bernoulli law only. The joint law is not determined by that marginal and exhibits an extra one-hot competition and persistent \(-1/q^2\) correlation. Older weighted Cayley/forest enumerators may implicitly give this formula, so historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The marked-path joint degrees are a natural statistic of uniform trees conditional on two-point distance; the previously published marginal does not determine their dependence. The exact q-variate law identifies topology-invariant simultaneous competition for one compulsory outside attachment. It yields a nonzero limiting negative covariance \(-1/q^2\) between any two fixed marked vertices despite asymptotically independent Poisson fluctuations, and a joint two-endpoint stochastic coupling. These are structural dependence facts for all q/n regimes, not a selected numerical special case or normalization test.
